characters.name: Frank Stoddard
characters.goal: maintain order and avoid mill shutdown

characters.name: Hettie Ward
characters.goal: find Callum after he missed his night shift return

characters.name: Declan Boyd
characters.goal: protect union yard workers from company blame

characters.name: Pete Noonan
characters.goal: keep elevator motors running without tripping breakers

scene_cards.dramatic_function: Establishes Callum's death in the elevator machinery and places criminal liability directly on Jesse.

char_stoddard.goal: maintain order and avoid mill shutdown

char_jesse.goal: prove boot failure was not maintenance negligence

char_stoddard.goal: hold jesse accountable for safety inspection

required_beats: Jesse discovers Callum Ward's body crushed in the elevator intake machinery.
Pete helps pry the jammed bucket free, while Jesse clears a loop of bleached twine from the gears.
Gault arrives furious about the stoppage, leaving fresh purple transfer ink on the ladder.
Stoddard takes the signed safety ledger and warns Jesse that he faces manslaughter charges.

scene_cards.dramatic_function: Reveals Callum was investigating illicit shipments and surfaces suspicious physical evidence among the yard hands.
required_beats: Jesse breaks the news of Callum's death to Hettie, who reveals Callum was watching for an illicit shipment on the siding.
Declan intervenes and defends himself while carrying Callum's pocketknife, claiming Callum lent it to him to cut boxcar seals.

scene_cards.dramatic_function: Corroborates suspicious midnight activity on the siding through an outside witness.
required_beats: Jesse questions Maybelle at the scale house.
Maybelle admits she heard metallic banging near midnight and saw a cloaked figure flee toward the rail siding.

scene_cards.dramatic_function: Uncovers evidence that the conveyor circuit was deliberately blown from the overhead console rather than malfunctioning on the floor.

char_pete.goal: keep elevator motors running without tripping breakers
prevent electrical fire in tripper motor

required_beats: Jesse and Pete inspect the substation switchbank for the cause of the conveyor stall.
Pete reveals that the Leg #4 tripper fuse blew at midnight and was manually tripped from the overhead console.

scene_cards.dramatic_function: Uncovers evidence of an off-the-books late-night grain transfer that contradicts the official elevator records.

char_jesse.goal: prove boot failure was not maintenance negligence

required_beats: Jesse searches Maybelle's wastepaper basket while she is distracted.
Jesse recovers and smooths a crumpled, unnumbered slip detailing an untracked midnight release of forty tons of feed grain.

scene_cards.dramatic_function: Establishes Declan as the prime suspect in the elevator failure by pinning an alibi-less silhouette to him.

char_stoddard.goal: hold jesse accountable for safety inspection

required_beats: Stoddard confronts Declan by the track switch about his whereabouts during the elevator breakdown.
Declan insists he was working the outer boxcars alone all night without supervision.
Stoddard identifies Declan's hooded jacket as matching the reported silhouette.

scene_cards.dramatic_function: Reveals Gault's active cover-up of the illicit run and turns the threat of criminal blame directly onto Jesse.

char_gault.goal: coerce jesse into taking the fall

required_beats: Jesse presents the unnumbered midnight slip to Gault.
Gault dismisses the paper as old scrap and locks it away.
Gault warns Jesse that pressing the issue will leave Jesse to hang for criminal neglect.

scene_cards.dramatic_function: Deflects the constable's rush to pin the sabotage on Declan by proving the illicit shipment left by road rather than rail.
required_beats: Stoddard arrests Declan for sabotage using union threats and Callum's pocketknife as evidence.
Declan protests that he is being framed.
Jesse compares the slip tare weights against siding cars to show Stoddard the midnight shipment moved by rubber-tired truck rather than rail.

scene_cards.dramatic_function: Declan is exonerated by the physical evidence, turning the law's full suspicion onto Jesse with an impending arrest deadline.

char_stoddard.goal: prepare criminal negligence warrant for jesse

required_beats: Stoddard tests Callum's knife against the latch plate and finds the brass blade cannot match the deep tool gouges.
Stoddard releases Declan and clears him of sabotage.
Stoddard informs Jesse that mechanical negligence falls solely on him and gives him until sundown before filing an arrest warrant.

scene_cards.dramatic_function: Jesse ties Gault directly to the midnight manifest through Maybelle's unattended stamp pad.

char_jesse.goal: expose gault as the midnight intruder

required_beats: Jesse inspects the scale house stamp pad and hears Maybelle explain she left the desk unattended at midnight.
Jesse connects the purple ink to Gault's stained cuff, realizing Gault forged the manifest himself.

scene_cards.dramatic_function: Jesse uncovers the mechanism of deliberate sabotage, proving Callum's death was murder rather than negligence.
required_beats: Jesse recovers the bleached twine loop from the rubble in the pit.
Jesse shows Pete how the twine rigged the bypass gate open to dump tons of spoiled grain directly onto Callum.

scene_cards.dramatic_function: Jesse presents conclusive electrical evidence to Stoddard that exposes Gault as the culprit.
required_beats: Jesse gathers Stoddard and Gault at the substation and demonstrates that the blown fuse required the master supervisory switch to be closed.
Jesse shows the master switch can only be operated from Gault's private locked console.
Stoddard confirms Gault holds the supervisory key on his personal ring.

scene_cards.dramatic_function: To turn Gault's legal capture into Jesse's ruinous professional undoing.
required_beats: Stoddard arrests Gault for Callum's murder and seizes the forged midnight manifests.
Gault records Jesse's pre-signed morning safety log to expose regulatory fraud.
Stoddard confirms the violation permanently ends Jesse's terminal license.

scene_cards.dramatic_function: To resolve Jesse's journey by parting him from his trade with his conscience restored.

char_jesse.goal: expose gault as the midnight intruder

required_beats: Jesse surrenders his brass foreman keys at the rail yard gate.
Hettie acknowledges his choice to expose Callum's killer despite the cost.
Jesse leaves the terminal behind, blacklisted but clear-minded.

metadata.title: The Choke in the Boot Pit
metadata.source: segmented from a Fabula-only package by gemini-3.8-flash

premise.logline: A mystery in a working town, where the person who has to find out what happened is also the person who will be blamed for it.

plot_shape.name: Mystery
plot_shape.central_question: What actually happened, and who is willing to say so?

phases.name: Disturbance
phases.purpose: A wrong surfaces and someone is obliged to look into it.

phases.name: Inquiry
phases.purpose: Evidence accumulates, most of it true and misread.

phases.name: Wrong turn
phases.purpose: A reading of the evidence that is coherent and wrong collapses.

phases.name: Solution
phases.purpose: The true account, assembled only from what the reader has already been shown.

phases.name: Cost
phases.purpose: What knowing costs the person who found out.

cast_roles.purpose: Carries the reader through the inquiry and pays its cost.
Has a reason to keep the true account from being assembled.
Holds one true piece and misunderstands its meaning.
The reason the question matters at all.

obligatory_moves: Every element of the true account is on the page before it is stated.
At least one true detail is shown early in a context that makes it look irrelevant.
The wrong reading is defensible on the evidence available when it is made.

repairs: model | seed_fact: "loc_constable_office" seeded as known by char_stoddard

events.summary: Jesse climbs down into the boot pit to clear an elevator choke and finds the body of young Callum Ward trapped under the jammed bucket intake.
events.dramatic_function: Disturbance: Establishes the fatal incident and traps Jesse at the center of the physical site.
beats: Jesse descends into the dark, grain-choked boot pit expecting a broken pulley.
Jesse digs through cracked corn to find Callum Ward crushed beneath the intake mouth.
Jesse recognizes that the conveyor was running when Callum entered the hopper.

state_changes.value: unclog elevator boot and free Callum

events.summary: Pete joins Jesse in the pit to lever the jammed pulley free, where Jesse pulls an oiled loop of bleached sisal twine from the gears and discards it as refuse.
events.dramatic_function: Disturbance: Plants the mechanical evidence of the bypassed hopper lock under the mundane guise of cleaning machine wreckage.
beats: Pete arrives with crowbars to help pry the crushed elevator bucket away.
Jesse disentangles a knotted loop of bleached sisal twine from the teeth of the bottom idler sprocket.
Jesse tosses the twine on the rubble pile, assuming it is packing debris from grain car unloading.

events.summary: Superintendent Gault and Constable Stoddard enter the pit, with Gault furiously berating Jesse for the halt while smearing purple transfer ink from his starched sleeve onto the ladder rail.
events.dramatic_function: Disturbance: Introduces the concealer and plants the transfer-ink stain while establishing supervisory hostility.
beats: Gault rushes down the iron ladder shouting about shipping contracts and dead cargo.
Jesse spots fresh purple weigh-station transfer ink smeared wet across Gault's right shirt cuff.
Gault asserts that Callum must have wandered into the pit drunk or reckless during the graveyard run.

events.summary: Constable Stoddard confiscates the shift safety ledger and informs Jesse that his pre-shift signature on the clean inspection sheet makes him legally liable for Callum's death.
events.dramatic_function: Disturbance: Seals the trap around Jesse, mandating that he solve the death to save himself from criminal negligence charges.
beats: Stoddard pulls Jesse's pre-signed morning safety sheet from the clipboard on the pit wall.
Stoddard points out that Jesse certified all safety interlocks on Leg #4 as fully functional.
Stoddard warns Jesse that without proof of third-party sabotage, Jesse faces manslaughter charges.

state_changes.value: prove boot failure was not maintenance negligence
hold jesse accountable for safety inspection

events.summary: Jesse climbs into the rail yard and meets Callum's sister Hettie, who accuses Jesse of running unsafe machines and reveals Callum feared something in the yard during his graveyard shift.
events.dramatic_function: Inquiry: Establishes the human cost of the death and Callum's state of mind prior to entering the boot.
beats: Jesse breaks the news of Callum's death to Hettie beside the coal trestle.
Hettie furiously rebukes Jesse for running dangerous high-speed machinery without spotters.
Hettie reveals Callum had stayed late after midnight to watch for an illicit shipment on the siding.

events.summary: Union yard loader Declan Boyd confronts Jesse on the siding, brandishing Callum's horn-handled pocketknife which Declan claims Callum lent him to cut grain-car seals.
events.dramatic_function: Inquiry: Introduces the prime red-herring suspect and plants Callum's bent knife.
beats: Declan steps between Jesse and Hettie, warning Jesse not to shift management blame onto workers.
Jesse sees Callum's recognizable horn-handled pocketknife sticking out of Declan's bib pocket.
Declan snaps open the bent, greasy blade and insists Callum gave it to him before midnight to pop boxcar seals.

events.summary: Jesse enters the scale house to question Maybelle, who admits she heard heavy iron latch banging near midnight and saw a cloaked figure running toward the rail siding.
events.dramatic_function: Inquiry: Adds witness testimony that seems to support the theory of an outside saboteur.
beats: Jesse finds Maybelle shaking at her desk, trying to align the weigh-scale tallies.
Maybelle recounts hearing metallic clatter by the outside chute shortly before the elevator stalled.
She reports seeing a hooded shape in work boots slip through the yard shadows toward the boxcars.

events.summary: Jesse checks the terminal electrical substation with Pete, discovering that the master remote control fuse for the Leg #4 tripper car blew out at midnight and was routinely swapped.
events.dramatic_function: Inquiry: Plants the technical anomaly of the master switchboard remote trigger.
beats: Jesse inspects the high-voltage switchbank to determine if an electrical short halted the conveyor.
Pete shows Jesse a scorched copper fuse plug removed from the remote tripper circuit.
Pete notes that someone tripped the circuit from the overhead console rather than the floor switch.

state_changes.value: prevent electrical fire in tripper motor

events.summary: Returning to the scale house, Jesse sifts through the waste bin and uncovers a crumpled, unnumbered freight slip detailing an unrecorded midnight grain loading.
events.dramatic_function: Inquiry: Plants the paper trail for off-book terminal commerce.
beats: Jesse searches Maybelle's wastepaper basket while she handles an incoming truck horn.
He smooths out a carbon slip recording forty tons of feed grain released without lot numbers.
The ticket bears a stamped time of 11:45 PM and an indecipherable clerk mark.

events.summary: In the rail yard, Constable Stoddard finds Declan loitering near the siding and begins interrogating him about his whereabouts when the elevator jammed.
events.dramatic_function: Inquiry: Heightens suspicion on the red-herring suspect as law enforcement focuses on Declan.
beats: Stoddard spots Declan wiping coal grease from his palms by the track switch.
Declan claims he worked the outer boxcars alone all night without an overseer.
Stoddard notes that Declan's work jacket matches the hooded silhouette described by Maybelle.

events.summary: Jesse takes the unnumbered manifest to Gault's office, where Gault flatly denies running any night freight and warns Jesse that pointing fingers will ensure Jesse hangs alone for criminal neglect.
events.dramatic_function: Inquiry: Establishes the concealer actively attempting to suppress evidence and intimidate the investigator.
beats: Jesse lays the crumpled midnight slip on Gault's mahogany desk.
Gault calls the paper a discarded mistake from last autumn and locks it in his desk drawer.
Gault reminds Jesse that the coroner will accept the signed maintenance sheet unless an outside culprit is jailed.

state_changes.value: coerce jesse into taking the fall

events.summary: Constable Stoddard intercepts Declan in the rail yard and arrests him, citing Declan's earlier union strike threats and Maybelle's midnight sighting as proof of deliberate sabotage.
events.dramatic_function: Wrong Turn: The coherent, defensible wrong theory peaks as law enforcement moves to close the case on Declan.
beats: Stoddard brandishes the union grievance letters where Declan swore the elevator would grind to a halt.
Stoddard seizes Callum's pocketknife from Declan's coat, calling it a stolen murder weapon.
Declan shouts that he was framed and demands that Jesse look at the physical locks.

events.summary: Jesse studies the duplicate slip numbers against the yard switch-list and demonstrates to Stoddard that the midnight shipment was a highway flatbed, not Declan's rail cars.
events.dramatic_function: Wrong Turn: Begins cracking the wrong theory by divorcing the midnight movement from the rail union.
beats: Jesse compares the unnumbered manifest tare weights with the empty siding boxcars.
Jesse shows Stoddard that the wheel-weights record tandem rubber tires, not iron rail bogies.
Stoddard realizes the grain moved outside Declan's union siding completely.

events.summary: In the boot pit, Stoddard attempts to fit Callum's bent knife blade into the forced emergency chute latch, but the soft brass blade cannot match the deep tool gouges.
events.dramatic_function: Wrong Turn: Collapses the wrong theory completely as the physical evidence refutes Declan's involvement.
beats: Stoddard presses the blade of Callum's knife against the scraped iron latch plate.
The soft horn-and-tin handle bends, showing the strike marks were gouged by heavy hardened alloy.
Stoddard admits the knife could never have forced the hardened hopper gate.

events.summary: With Declan exonerated, Stoddard orders Declan released and informs Jesse that he is drafting the formal negligence warrant against Jesse as the solely liable party.
events.dramatic_function: Wrong Turn: Resolves the collapse of the false lead by turning all institutional force directly back onto the investigator.
beats: Stoddard removes Declan's restraints and orders him out of the pit.
Stoddard tells Jesse that absent sabotage, mechanical neglect under Jesse's signature is the only charge left.
Jesse is given until sundown before the arrest warrant is filed with the county magistrate.

state_changes.value: prepare criminal negligence warrant for jesse

events.summary: Jesse inspects the midnight logbook in the scale house and connects the purple transfer ink on Maybelle's stamp pad to the fresh stain he saw on Gault's cuff.
events.dramatic_function: Solution: Assembles the first piece of the true account by proving the superintendent altered records in person.
beats: Jesse examines the purple indelible transfer ink used only on official gross-weight stamps.
Maybelle admits she left the stamp desk unattended for ten minutes at midnight to check the track whistle.
Jesse realizes Gault's stained shirt sleeve proves Gault stamped the midnight manifest himself.

state_changes.value: expose gault as the midnight intruder

events.summary: In the boot pit, Jesse retrieves the discarded loop of bleached twine and demonstrates to Pete how it had been rigged to hold open the emergency grain bypass chute.
events.dramatic_function: Solution: Assembles the physical mechanics of the murder from early evidence.
beats: Jesse picks the loop of bleached twine out of the pit rubble.
He hooks the looped knot over the bypass gate lever, proving it held the gate open against safety springs.
Pete realizes someone deliberately routed twenty tons of spoiled top-bin grain straight down into the boot where Callum was inspecting.

events.summary: Jesse summons Stoddard and Gault to the electrical substation, proving from the blown midnight remote fuse that the tripper was switched on from Gault's private overhead console.
events.dramatic_function: Solution: Completes the true account and corners the concealer before legal authority.
beats: Jesse points out that the blown tripper fuse only completes a circuit when the master supervisory switch is closed.
Jesse demonstrates that the overhead switch is locked inside Gault's private keybox.
Stoddard checks Gault's brass key ring and finds the supervisory key on his chain.

events.summary: In the mill office, Stoddard snaps irons on Gault for Callum's murder, but Gault uses Jesse's pre-signed morning safety sheet to legally force Jesse's immediate firing and blacklisting.
events.dramatic_function: Cost: The truth is established, but the formal violation committed by the investigator extracts its legal penalty.
beats: Stoddard reads Gault his rights and secures the forged midnight manifests from the wall safe.
Gault spitefully enters Jesse's pre-signed safety log into the county record, documenting regulatory fraud.
Stoddard confirms that under terminal law, signing an uninspected safety ledger terminates Jesse's license forever.

events.summary: Jesse surrenders his terminal keys at the siding gate and receives Hettie's quiet acknowledgment before walking out of the terminal blacklisted and jobless.
events.dramatic_function: Cost: Closes the arc on the investigator paying the personal cost of bringing the truth to light.
beats: Jesse lays his brass foreman keys on the yard gate pedestal.
Hettie stops him at the tracks, acknowledging that Jesse risked prison to name Callum's true killer.
Jesse walks past the idle grain elevators into town with his trade gone and his conscience clear.
